description.short: This British soul singer is never gonna let you down.
description.standard: Rick Astley's 1987 debut, Whenever You Need Somebody, put an of-the-moment spin on the Motown ideal; hitmakers Stock Aitken Waterman paired Astley's vocal with sparkling synth-pop on smashes like the joyous “Together Forever” and the giddily devoted “Never Gonna Give You Up.” After Astley broke with SAW, his smooth yet strong voice gave urgency to the gospel-tinged “Cry for Help” and the wrenching “Hopelessly.” In the mid-'00s, “Never” returned via the fake-out meme known as “Rickrolling”; not long after, Astley came back as well, stripping down on “Keep Singing” and heading to the disco on “Beautiful Life.”

description.short: Hear what was trending on radio stations around the world in 2024.
description.standard: All year long, Shazam’s music recognition technology tracked what songs were being played on radio stations around the world. (That’s nearly 1 million hours of music each day, broadcasting on more than 40,000 stations from Sacramento to Stockholm to Seoul.) Country music came up huge worldwide in 2024: Among the year’s top 20 most-played songs were breakthrough hits from Dasha and Shaboozey and Beyoncé’s country crossover. Sabrina Carpenter ends a banner year with a trio of Top 100 hits (“Feather,” “Please Please Please,” “Espresso”). But the queen of the airwaves was Dua Lipa, who nabs the No. 1 spot, plus five more entries on the list. Hear what else the world listened to this year.

description.short: Floor-fillers from the MTV era’s mash-up of pop, hip-hop, and rock.
description.standard: In the ’80s, the future was so bright, everyone not only had to wear shades—they were compelled to head to the dance floor, where beat-forward jams could be found in any section of the record store. While artists like Madonna and Michael Jackson made getting into the groove their music’s top priority, the always-on attitude of the ’80s meant that any pop artist, no matter what genre their music was rooted in, could be a remix away from helping people express themselves through movement. Duran Duran’s glossy New Wave, Janet Jackson’s fiery anthems, Run-DMC’s booming beats, INXS’ sinewy sax-rock, Prince’s hyperactive funk, George Michael’s sex-positive soul, and Cyndi Lauper’s retro-nouveau pop all electrified dance floors, whether they were in high-class clubs or streamer-decorated school gymnasiums—and they still sound vital decades after they first lit up the charts.

description.short: The decade when synths and videos took pop to new heights.
description.standard: An irresistible synth melody. A snare drum loaded with reverb. A guitar line that’s tight and powerful. If the song you’re listening to has at least one of these things, it may be from the 1980s, the decade when disco waned and hip-hop emerged, Madonna blew up in the U.S., the hitmaking team of Stock Aitken Waterman pumped out smash singles for Rick Astley and Dead or Alive, and Michael Jackson broke sales and chart records around the world. Of course, thanks to MTV, this was also a decade when the biggest stars weren't just heard but also seen, as the music video gave artists a new medium to explore. Peter Gabriel mastered the form with psychedelic mini-masterpieces to complement his vibrant art-pop, while Prince, in the midst of reinventing rock ’n’ roll, turned out two feature-length film masterpieces with classic soundtracks to match.

description.short: Hear what was trending on pop radio stations around the world in 2024.
description.standard: All year long, Shazam’s music recognition technology tracked what songs were being played on radio stations around the world. (That’s nearly 1 million hours of music each day, broadcasting on more than 40,000 stations from Sacramento to Stockholm to Seoul.) Five of the year’s 25 most-played pop songs belonged to Dua Lipa, including three from her third studio album, Radical Optimism. Miley Cyrus’ “Flowers” stayed in heavy rotation, while the award for the year’s biggest pop breakthrough goes to Sabrina Carpenter, who ends 2024 with three songs on the list. Hear what else the world listened to this year.

description.short: An era- and genre-spanning playlist of the most universal songs in pop.
description.standard: Here’s an era- and genre-spanning playlist of genuine pop classics—the stuff of weddings and barbecues, that transcends old and young; songs so deeply lodged in the cultural memory that you can probably hum them even if you don’t know their names. In other words, music we know, love, and never get tired of. Evergreen as most of this stuff is, our editors do make updates regularly, so if you hear something you like, add it to your library.

description.standard: From reserved Quiet Storm balladry to over-the-top devotionals that sounded even better in arenas, romance buoyed the ‘80s pop landscape. Massive superstars, weepy belters, smooth soul singers, notoriously mopey rock heroes—no one was immune to Cupid's charms, and the love songs of that decade remain dedication-worthy years later.
